name: Rutersju Twelve
summary: A 12-deal trick-taking game: each player is dealt 3 cards, players bid 0 to 3 in turn, the highest bidder plays to take exactly that many tricks, and the opponents score when the declarer misses.

player.meaning: Cards held this deal, such as 'AS' or '7D'. Only the owner sees them.
Whether this player is the declarer this deal.

game.initial: all 36 cards: ranks A,K,Q,J,10,9,8,7,6 in suits S,H,D,C
game.meaning: Undealt cards. They stay unseen for the whole deal.
Number of the current deal, from 1 to 12.
Seat that bids first this deal.
Highest bid made so far this deal.
Seat of the declarer this deal.
Number of tricks completed this deal.
Seat that leads the current trick.
Suit of the first card in the current trick.
Entries of the form seat:card for the trick in progress.
Every card played this deal, visible to everyone.

setup: Seats are numbered 1 to N in clockwise order.
Every player's score is set to 0.

round.effect: Add 1 to deal_number. Set first_bidder = ((deal_number - 1) mod N) + 1. Refill deck with all 36 cards. For every player, clear hand and set bid = 0, tricks = 0 and is_declarer = false. Set high_bid = -1, declarer_seat = 0, contract = 0, trick_number = 0 and led_suit = ''. Clear trick_cards and played_cards.
Deal 3 cards to each player. Each card is drawn at random from deck, appended to that player's hand and removed from deck.
Each player is shown their own hand, plus deal_number, first_bidder and every score.

round.who: each player in turn, clockwise, starting at first_bidder
round.effect: Set the player's bid to the answer and broadcast it to all. If bid >= high_bid, set high_bid = bid and declarer_seat = the player's seat. Because the comparison is >=, a later equal bid takes the declarership.
Set contract = high_bid and leader_seat = declarer_seat. Set is_declarer = true for the player at declarer_seat. Announce the declarer and the contract.

round.who: each player in turn, clockwise, starting at leader_seat
round.answer: one card from the player's hand, chosen from the legal cards (see offers)
round.effect: Remove the card from hand and append seat:card to trick_cards and to played_cards. If this is the first card of the trick, set led_suit to its suit. Broadcast the played card to all.

If trick_cards contains 7D, its player wins the trick. Otherwise the highest-ranked card of led_suit wins (A>K>Q>J>10>9>8>7>6). Add 1 to the winner's tricks, set leader_seat = the winner's seat, add 1 to trick_number, clear trick_cards and set led_suit = ''. Announce the trick winner.
Run the two previous steps (play a trick, resolve the trick) again until trick_number = 3.

Let D be the player with is_declarer = true. If D.tricks = contract, add contract + 1 to D.score. Otherwise add |contract - D.tricks| to the score of every player with is_declarer = false, and D scores nothing. Opponents' own tricks are not scored.
Announce every player's score after deal {deal_number}.
End the game if deal_number = 12. Otherwise continue with the next deal.

ending.condition: deal_number = 12 after the 12th deal is scored
ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their total score after 12 deals. The highest total wins. Players tied for the highest total share the result, which the source calls a draw.

rules.text: When a game starts, then every player's score is 0.
When a deal starts, then all 36 cards are shuffled into deck and each player receives exactly 3 cards in hand, seen only by that player.
When cards are dealt, then the 36 - 3N undealt cards stay in deck, unseen by every player for the whole deal.
When deal 1 starts, then seat 1 bids first; when deal k > 1 starts, then the first bidder is the seat clockwise from the previous first bidder, so first_bidder = ((k - 1) mod N) + 1.
When bidding, then every player bids exactly once, in clockwise order from first_bidder, with a whole number from 0 to 3, and there is no pass.
When a bid is made, then it is shown to every player at once.
When bidding ends, then the player with the highest bid is declarer and contract equals that bid.
When two or more players tie for the highest bid, then the one of them who bid last is declarer (for example, bids 2, 2, 1, 0 in bidding order make the second bidder declarer).
When the first trick of a deal begins, then the declarer leads it.
When a player holds a card of the led suit, then that player must play a card of the led suit.
When a player holds no card of the led suit, then that player may play any card in hand.
When the diamond 7 is in a trick, then its player wins the trick, whatever suit was led.
When the diamond 7 is not in a trick, then the highest card of the led suit wins, ranking A>K>Q>J>10>9>8>7>6, and cards of other suits never win.
When a trick is won, then the winner's tricks increases by 1 and the winner leads the next trick.
When a deal is played, then exactly 3 tricks are played, and every played card stays visible to all players.
When the declarer's tricks equal the contract, then the declarer scores contract + 1 (a contract of 0 made scores 1, a contract of 3 made scores 4) and the opponents score 0.
When the declarer's tricks differ from the contract, then each opponent scores |contract - declarer tricks| and the declarer scores 0 (for example, contract 3 with 1 trick gives each opponent 2).
When scoring, then opponents' own tricks add nothing.
When a deal is scored, then every player's total is announced.
When the 12th deal is scored, then the game ends and the highest total score wins; if several players tie for the highest total, the game is a draw.
When playing, then no player may send a message; players communicate only through bids and cards.

offers.question: Bid
offers.who: each player in turn from first_bidder
offers.options: Every player is offered 0, 1, 2 or 3. No pass is offered.

offers.question: Play a card (leader of a trick)
Play a card (non-leader)
offers.who: each other seat in clockwise order
offers.options: A seat holding one or more cards of led_suit is offered only those cards. A seat holding no card of led_suit is offered every card in its hand.

choices.why: The source allows 3 to 4 and the designer chose 4. Three is the smallest table with more than one opponent to set the contract against. More than 4 would exceed the 36-card pack's balance and make each trick too crowded for a 3-card hand to steer.
The rules forbid discussion; players communicate only through bids and cards.
A text code per card lets the engine check suits and ranks arithmetically.

choices.what: Declarer tie-break done by updating on bid >= high_bid in bidding order
choices.why: This makes the last of the tied highest bidders the declarer, exactly as the rules require, using only arithmetic.

A thoughtful player bids from hand strength and from the bids already made, since bidding last wins ties. Opponents cooperate to break the contract, either by taking tricks from the declarer or by giving tricks away when the declarer bid low.

simplifications.what: The source's draw on a tied top total is represented as a shared win among the tied players
simplifications.why: The engine has no separate draw; players level at the top share the result.

simplifications.what: The 3-trick play loop is expressed as a repeat over two steps
simplifications.why: The engine runs flat step lists and repeats them until a condition holds.
